chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Umar ibn Muslim al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Bashir al-Hamadani, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah - in a tradition from which we have condensed the point of need - that he said:

Indeed, for the people of so-and-so there is a kingdom appointed for a term. When they feel secure and at ease, and think that their kingdom will not cease, a cry will be raised among them, and no leader will remain to gather them, nor a caller to be heard by them.

"Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought."

I said: May I be your ransom, is there a fixed time for that? He replied: No, because the knowledge of Allah surpasses the knowledge of those who fix times. Indeed, Allah the Exalted promised Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten, which Musa did not know, nor did the Children of Israel know. So when the time passed, they said: Musa has deceived us! And they worshipped the calf. But when need and poverty increase among the people, and one denies another, then at that time expect the command of Allah morning and evening.

key_terms.الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا: the earth takes on its adornment
key_terms.رَاعٍ: a leader or shepherd who gathers
key_terms.مَلْكًا مُؤَجَّلًا: an appointed kingdom with a fixed term
key_terms.وَاعٍ: a caller or announcer who is heard

ai.seo_question: When will the divine command arrive and how do we know the time is near?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* elucidates the unpredictability of the Imam’s reappearance by contrasting human certainty with divine knowledge, citing the calf incident as a precedent for sudden judgment after a promised period. It links the eschatological 'unexpected command' to Quran 10:24, emphasizing that while the exact hour is hidden, social decay and widespread hardship serve as reliable indicators for believers to anticipate divine intervention.
